column1: # Nix definitions. Rule (narrow: an attribute set declares nothing as such, so only what a file binds at its top level counts):

#  - the top level is the expression the file evaluates to, looking through `{ args }:` and `x:` function layers, then either the bindings of a top-level `let .. in`, or the attributes of the `{ }` / `rec { }` that is the file's body (or the body of that let);
#  - a binding with a single-name path is a function when its value is a function (double = x: x * 2) and a variable otherwise;

#  - not definitions: dotted paths (options.a.b = ..), quoted names, inherit, anything nested inside a value (the keys of an inner set, a nested let), function parameters, and files whose body is not a set or a let (default.nix here).
